comparisons.peer_topic: Hyperscale Customer Base and Product Applications
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's data center products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, and adaptive SOCs, are purchased by large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers. These customers incorporate the products into servers for web applications, public cloud services, and AI workloads such as generative AI models.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe their data center AI businesses in the context of serving cloud providers, but they differ in product offering and delivery model. NVDA focuses on a managed 'AI-training-as-a-service' platform (DGX Cloud) where it hosts software and expertise, whereas AMD describes its role as a hardware supplier where cloud providers incorporate its GPU accelerators into servers. NVDA's strategy involves a service layer hosted by partners, while AMD's strategy involves component sales for integration by OEMs/ODMs.

sentences.text: In fiscal year 2024, we launched the NVIDIA DGX Cloud, an AI-training-as-a-service platform which includes cloud-based infrastructure and software for AI, customizable pretrained AI models, and access to NVIDIA experts.
We have partnered with leading cloud service providers to host this service in their data centers.

Large multi-national public cloud service providers and hyperscale private data centers directly and indirectly purchase a substantial portion of our data center-focused products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs and Adaptive SOCs.

These products are incorporated into servers and other data center appliances sold by OEMs to the hyperscale customers or into custom servers or hardware designed by or for these customers and manufactured by ODMs or contract manufacturers.

peer_results.rationale: AVGO candidates (private cloud software, Telco Cloud) focus on infrastructure software and telecom network modernization, which does not match NVDA's specific disclosure of launching an AI-training-as-a-service platform (DGX Cloud).

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Intel launched the Intel Gaudi 3 AI accelerators, offering significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight the launch of new AI accelerator products in 2024 as a key business driver in their data center segments. NVDA launched the DGX Cloud platform to offer AI training as a service, while Intel launched the Gaudi 3 AI accelerators. The similarity lies in the 2024 launch of new AI-capable infrastructure offerings; the difference is in the nature of the offering, with NVDA providing a comprehensive training service platform and Intel providing hardware accelerators focused on inference price-performance.

comparisons.peer_summary: CNBU data center sales were driven by server demand in cloud and enterprise markets, with growth fueled by the shift of infrastructure and workloads to the cloud and the memory-intensive nature of AI data-centric workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the growth drivers in the data center market related to AI, but from different layers of the stack. NVDA describes its strategic launch of a software and service platform (DGX Cloud) for AI training, while Micron describes the hardware demand drivers (memory) for AI workloads. Both identify AI as a primary growth engine for their respective data center businesses, with NVDA focusing on the compute/service layer and Micron on the memory/storage layer (HBM/DRAM) required to support these AI data-centric workloads.

sentences.text: In fiscal year 2024, we launched the NVIDIA DGX Cloud, an AI-training-as-a-service platform which includes cloud-based infrastructure and software for AI, customizable pretrained AI models, and access to NVIDIA experts.
